item.title: Alleged Fijian figure in Sydney crime gang detained in Dubai
item.description: A man identified as the alleged head of a Sydney-based criminal group with Fijian links has reportedly been detained in Dubai while travelling to Lebanon. According to Australia’s Daily Telegraph, Joseph Vokai was detained by authorities in the United Arab Emirates during a stopover and has been held without charge for the past week.
item.content:encoded:
A man identified as the alleged head of a Sydney-based criminal group with Fijian links has reportedly been detained in Dubai while travelling to Lebanon.

According to Australia’s Daily Telegraph, Joseph Vokai was detained by authorities in the United Arab Emirates during a stopover and has been held without charge for the past week.

The newspaper reports that Vokai is the alleged leader of the KVT, a Sydney-based group it says is dominated by Fijian members.

The report states that Vokai was travelling to visit members of the Alameddine crime clan in Lebanon when he was detained.

The Daily Telegraph says Vokai is the latest in a series of Sydney-based crime figures detained by Dubai authorities as the UAE steps up action against individuals suspected of links to organised crime.

According to the newspaper, several other alleged Australian underworld figures have also been detained or removed from the UAE in recent months.

The report quotes a senior New South Wales Police source as saying authorities were aware of Vokai’s detention.

“We share intelligence with all international law enforcement agencies around the world,” the source was quoted as saying.

The source added that the Australian Federal Police also plays an active role in ensuring overseas authorities are aware of individuals suspected of involvement in organised crime.

The Daily Telegraph further reported that law enforcement agencies are increasingly working with international partners to disrupt the activities of alleged criminal syndicates operating across multiple countries.

Authorities in the UAE and Australia have not publicly announced any criminal charges against Vokai in relation to the reported detention.

item.title: EFL receives $15.6M insurance settlement for cyclone-damaged wind farm
item.description: Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) received the balance of a $15.6 million insurance settlement in 2025 following extensive damage to its Butoni Wind Farm caused by Tropical Cyclone Harold. According to EFL’s 2025 Annual Report, recently tabled in Parliament, the company completed major restoration work on the wind farm after accepting the insurer’s final settlement offer.
item.content:encoded:
Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) received the balance of a $15.6 million insurance settlement in 2025 following extensive damage to its Butoni Wind Farm caused by Tropical Cyclone Harold.

According to EFL’s 2025 Annual Report, recently tabled in Parliament, the company completed major restoration work on the wind farm after accepting the insurer’s final settlement offer.

The Butoni Wind Farm, commissioned in 2007, sustained significant damage when Tropical Cyclone Harold struck Fiji on 7 April 2020.

Following a comprehensive damage assessment conducted by Vergnet, EFL lodged an insurance claim under its Material Damage/Business Interruption (MD/BI) insurance policy in 2024.

The report states that EFL’s Board approved the insurer’s final settlement offer of $15.6 million, net of deductibles, in December 2024. Formal acceptance of the offer was completed in February 2025, in accordance with the insurer’s requirements.

EFL had already received $4.5 million in 2024, with the remaining $11.1 million paid during the 2025 financial year.

The company said the funding enabled repair works to restore the wind farm to its original operating condition and resulted in the reversal of a previously recognised impairment loss of $3.08 million.

According to the report, 20 wind turbines have now been repaired and recommissioned.

However, work remains ongoing on the remaining 15 wind turbines, which had not yet been recommissioned when the 2025 financial statements were authorised.

EFL said the restoration of the Butoni Wind Farm forms part of its ongoing efforts to strengthen Fiji’s renewable energy infrastructure and improve the resilience of the national electricity network.

item.title: 2026-2027 budget guide in three languages launched
item.description: Fijians will now have easier access to information on how public money is raised, allocated and spent following the launch of the Citizens’ Guide to the National Budget 2026–2027. The simplified publication, released by the Ministry of Finance, is available for the second consecutive year in English, iTaukei and Hindi, making the National Budget more accessible, transparent and inclusive.
item.content:encoded:
Fijians will now have easier access to information on how public money is raised, allocated and spent following the launch of the Citizens’ Guide to the National Budget 2026–2027.

The simplified publication, released by the Ministry of Finance, is available for the second consecutive year in English, iTaukei and Hindi, making the National Budget more accessible, transparent and inclusive.

Minister for Finance, Commerce and Business Development Esrom Immanuel said the guide is aimed at helping people from all backgrounds understand the Government’s priorities and how Budget decisions affect their daily lives.

“Today marks yet another significant milestone in our journey of making the National Budget more accessible, transparent and inclusive for all Fijians,” Mr Immanuel said.

He said the 2026–2027 National Budget, themed “A Responsible Budget for a Sustainable Future,” reflects the aspirations of the people following extensive public consultations and is built on responsible financial management.

According to the Minister, the Budget is designed to support sustainable economic growth while protecting vulnerable households.

“This initiative is about much more than translation. It is about ensuring that every citizen, regardless of language or background, has the opportunity to engage with the Budget, understand the Government’s priorities, and appreciate how public resources are being invested to improve their lives,” he said.

Mr Immanuel acknowledged the Ministry of iTaukei Affairs, Culture, Heritage and Arts for assisting with the iTaukei translation of the guide.

He also thanked Permanent Secretary for Finance Shiri Gounder, Head of Fiscal Policy Munesh Deo and the Ministry’s Fiscal Policy team for producing the publication in all three languages.

The Citizens’ Guide to the National Budget 2026–2027 is now available in English, iTaukei and Hindi through the Ministry of Finance.

item.title: FSC offers prime Momi property for sale by tender
item.description: The Fiji Sugar Corporation (FSC) is inviting written tenders for the sale of a 7.8-acre freehold property in Momi, Nadroga, describing the site as having strong residential, commercial and tourism development potential. According to a public advertisement, the property comprises Freehold Land CT 4057, Lot 1 N39, Momi, Nadroga, with a total land area of 31,565.48 square metres (7.8 acres).
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Sugar Corporation (FSC) is inviting written tenders for the sale of a 7.8-acre freehold property in Momi, Nadroga, describing the site as having strong residential, commercial and tourism development potential.

According to a public advertisement, the property comprises Freehold Land CT 4057, Lot 1 N39, Momi, Nadroga, with a total land area of 31,565.48 square metres (7.8 acres).

FSC says the site is located in a central area of Momi, also known locally as Savusavu, approximately 45 minutes’ drive from Nadi International Airport.

The corporation highlights the property’s proximity to key amenities and tourism attractions, including Cloudbreak surf break and the Fiji Marriott Resort Momi Bay.

Existing improvements on the property include a single-storey building, the Savusavu Temple, and two residential houses.

The advertisement states that the property is surrounded by Savusavu Primary School, Momi Surf Charters, Tambua Sundry, and the Fiji Marriott Resort Momi Bay.

FSC says the land is suitable for a range of future developments, including a boutique resort or eco-lodge, a residential subdivision, or a private estate or community facility.

The corporation describes the site as being in a quiet and peaceful location with excellent potential for residential, commercial or mixed-use development, noting that its strategic location near educational facilities, tourism businesses and local services makes it attractive for investors.

Interested buyers have been invited to submit written tender offers in accordance with the requirements outlined in the advertisement.

item.title: FCCC targets cartels
item.description: BUSINESSES suspected of operating as cartels could face stronger action, with proposed changes to competition laws aimed at making it easier for the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC) to take alleged price-fixing and anti-competitive behaviour to court. A cartel occurs when two or more businesses work together instead of competing, often through agreements such as fixing prices or l
item.content:encoded:
BUSINESSES suspected of operating as cartels could face stronger action, with proposed changes to competition laws aimed at making it easier for the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC) to take alleged price-fixing and anti-competitive behaviour to court.

A cartel occurs when two or more businesses work together instead of competing, often through agreements such as fixing prices or limiting competition.

Under the current FCCC Act 2010, cartel-like behaviour can involve businesses secretly agreeing to fix prices or restrict competition, potentially resulting in consumers paying higher prices without knowing the market has been affected.

This is a challenge as FCCC needs to establish that a commitment was made or an agreement was acted upon.

FCCC chief executive Senikavika Jiuta said the proposed changes would remove the need to prove that businesses had taken a clear action or made a formal commitment after agreeing to limit competition.

“The element of commitment is now removed,” she told The Fiji Times.

“These proposed changes would allow discussions between businesses that demonstrate an intention to reduce competition to be considered in legal action.”

Ms Jiuta said the current law did not clearly define cartel-like behaviour, making it difficult for FCCC to build cases and resulting in limited court precedent.

“You’ll see there’s not much jurisprudence in court, or in high court or magistrates’ court, when we take these matters.”

She said the proposed changes would also provide FCCC with additional powers and tools to investigate alleged cartel activity and bring cases before the courts.

“So simply businessmen sitting at a restaurant and discussing this, we can take them to court.”

She added that FCCC currently had several cartels matters under review, including two investigations, but limitations under the existing legal framework affected how far the commission could proceed.

item.title: RFMF, agencies unite for major exercise
item.description: THE Republic of Fiji Military Forces will amplify and test its readiness to respond to national crises alongside other government agencies through Exercise Bougainville 2026. The exercise is intended to assess how government agencies work together during major emergencies by testing their coordination, communication and decision-making under simulated crisis scenarios.
item.content:encoded:
THE Republic of Fiji Military Forces will amplify and test its readiness to respond to national crises alongside other government agencies through Exercise Bougainville 2026.

The exercise is intended to assess how government agencies work together during major emergencies by testing their coordination, communication and decision-making under simulated crisis scenarios.

Speaking during the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with participating agencies, exercise lead planner Captain Seci Nawalowalo said the exercise was the culmination of six months of planning and had already been shaped by lessons from earlier tabletop and command post exercises.

He said the strategic objective had remained unchanged since planning began in February, with the exercise focused on validating the RFMF’s ability to support an inter-agency crisis response under a multi-agency coordination arrangement.

“The purpose is to test ourselves and provide opportunities for other agencies to evaluate our inter-agency mechanisms,” he said.

“Exercise Bougainville 2026 will run from August 7 to 28 and combine command post, tabletop and field training activities involving about 660 personnel from seven government agencies.

“The simulated scenarios will increase in complexity over five phases, beginning with humanitarian assistance and disaster relief operations before progressing to counter-terrorism and maritime operations.”

According to Capt Nawalowalo, the exercise is designed to expose participating agencies to a range of national security and emergency situations requiring a coordinated government response.

He said the exercise was not solely aimed at assessing the military’s operational capability but also at strengthening the way government agencies work together during national crises.

Captain Seci Nawalowalo during the signing of the memorandum of understanding for Exercise Bougainville 2026 at the Ministry’s Strategic headquarters in Suva yesterday. Picture: JONACANI LALAKOBAU

item.title: UK-style porn ban urged at consultation
item.description: Fiji must follow England’s lead and implement a total ban on internet pornography to combat a disturbing rise in incest and domestic sexual offences, local police and community members urge. The call to action was raised during a recent community consultation in Nasoso, Nadi, where residents and law enforcement noted that strict UK-style internet filtering could help protect vulnerable children in
item.content:encoded:
Fiji must follow England’s lead and implement a total ban on internet pornography to combat a disturbing rise in incest and domestic sexual offences, local police and community members urge.

The call to action was raised during a recent community consultation in Nasoso, Nadi, where residents and law enforcement noted that strict UK-style internet filtering could help protect vulnerable children inside Fijian homes.

“There are a lot of pilots in Nasoso, and one of the pilots suggested that if England blocked watching of pornographic movies, then why can’t we?” said Sergeant Semi Meru of the Namaka Police Station.

“The pilot was sharing that in England, if you go to Google, and if you start to search pornography, it is totally blocked.”

The push for tighter internet controls comes amid alarming new data. Mid-year statistics released by the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions revealed 37 rape or sexual assault incidents involving relatives or people in domestic relationships between January and June.

Among these cases were seven involving the sexual abuse of stepchildren.

In another horrific incident in June, a 56-year-old man was charged with raping his 13-year-old biological daughter.

Sgt Meru stated that the increase in father-daughter sexual offences is directly linked to increased exposure to explicit online content.

He warned that easy access to pornography distorts behaviour within the household, leading to opportunistic and devastating abuse against children.

“If a father rapes his own daughter, then we know maybe the father was watching it,” Sgt Meru explained.

He said Fiji may be a small nation but the rise of sexual offences within families was a major crisis that requires immediate, nationwide intervention.

item.title: Saurogo: Protect our elders
item.description: FIJI is facing a heartbreaking crisis behind closed doors as our cherished elders are increasingly forgotten, exploited, and abandoned by their own flesh and blood. Speaking at a World in Art and Climate Action (WACA) roundtable discussion in Lautoka yesterday, administrator Paulini Saurogo laid bare the deeply concerning realities confronting the nation’s senior citizens.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI is facing a heartbreaking crisis behind closed doors as our cherished elders are increasingly forgotten, exploited, and abandoned by their own flesh and blood.

Speaking at a World in Art and Climate Action (WACA) roundtable discussion in Lautoka yesterday, administrator Paulini Saurogo laid bare the deeply concerning realities confronting the nation’s senior citizens.

The event coincided with the World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly, marking the prophet Isaiah’s poignant words: “I will never forget you.”

She said the theme reminded people that God’s love for every person never fails – even in the fragility of old age.

Yet, current data reveals a painful departure from traditional Fijian values of communal care.

While general crimes against citizens over 60 dropped 13.6 per cent from 1945 cases in 2024 to 1680 in 2025, sinister threats are on the rise.

Financial exploitation has skyrocketed by a staggering 86 per cent, with fraud cases jumping from 29 cases in 2024 to 54 cases last year.

“We have also recorded 159 cases of assault causing actual bodily harm against older persons, along with incidents involving criminal intimidation, trespass, online-related offences, and money laundering targeting elderly victims.

“The Western Division, where we are gathered today, has recorded the highest number of elderly victims, while the Northern Division has seen an overall increase in cases.”

Beyond the cold statistics lies a hidden, psychological torment.

Shockingly, two-thirds of all reported abusers are the victims’ own adult children.

Furthermore, a growing number of families are opting to place their parents and grandparents into aged care facilities rather than looking after them at home.

Ms Saurogo urged the public to confront this hidden suffering, stressing that senior citizens are a precious blessing entitled to live with dignity, safety, and respect, rather than being cast aside as a burden.
